thesis: The speakers discuss the unique dynamic of Bill Ford serving as both a former chair of the Rockefeller University investment committee and a manager whose firm, General Atlantic, was previously ineligible for investment due to a conflict of interest policy. They note that the firm's performance at scale was a pleasant surprise, as size is typically the enemy of returns, and highlight Bill Ford's consistent facilitation style and ability to make committee members feel a sense of ownership.
